note: Machine-checkable closure ledger. Every row carries a predicate that returns true when the defect is PRESENT at HEAD. `node scripts/check-bottlenecks.mjs` fails when a row marked `closed` still fires (REOPENED), when a row marked `open` no longer fires (FIXED_UNRECORDED), or when a row marked `refuted` fires (REFUTED_BUT_PRESENT). Rows here replace the prose findings list: a claim that cannot be machine-checked is a row with `kind: "manual"`, which is re-verified rather than trusted. Never delete a `refuted` row — it is what stops a dead finding from being re-derived.

rows.title: REFUTED: a tracked launcher imports modules that live in gitignored .canary/tools
rows.evidence: False at HEAD. scripts/run-electron.cjs already imported ./lib/atomic-record.mjs and ./lib/process-identity.mjs; the 7 canary modules are already tracked under scripts/lib/; and .canary/ is only partially ignored — 24 files under it are tracked, including canary-run.mjs, canary-session.mjs, fifteen-pages-run.mjs, phase4-verify.mjs and viewport-run.mjs, all of which already imported ../../scripts/lib/. The finding came from a worktree divergence: the local working copy still carried the pre-migration ../.canary/tools/ paths while HEAD had already migrated. Restoring the worktree to the committed paths made the claim disappear, which is why this row is kept — it is precisely the 'prose finding outlives the fix' pathology this ledger exists to stop.

rows.title: The MCP proxy's client dispatch ceiling could fall below the server's largest policy budget with no gate to notice
rows.evidence: The proxy carried a hand-maintained CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS table (8 entries, 30 s default) while the catalogue grew to a 180 s policy (browser.visual_compare). theme.debug_bundle carried a 60 s policy with no table entry, so the 30 s default fired first, and the human-read verdict at .canary/CORE-BOTTLENECKS.md:402 had already recorded this class as fixed.
rows.closedBy: The per-tool table is deleted; the proxy owns one ceiling (DEFAULT_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 240000) and scripts/check-mcp-budget-dominance.mjs runs inside `compile`, builds the real catalogue, and fails when the ceiling stops dominating the largest policy, when a per-tool table reappears, or when a routing row is a no-op.

rows.title: anti.browser.tabs.list was routed to a session-scoped capability, so the advertised window-wide default never ran
rows.evidence: The proxy advertised `all: { default: true }` while CAPABILITY_MAP rewrote the name to browser.list-tabs, whose handler is session-scoped unless `all` is truthy, and the proxy never applies JSON-Schema defaults. Live probes: `{}` returned the bound tab only, `{all: true}` returned the window strip.
rows.closedBy: The routing row is deleted, so the advertised name reaches the catalogue's own anti.browser.tabs.list (window-wide unless all === false), and an E2E case in test/main/omp-mcp-adapter.test.ts asserts the dispatched name.

predicate.pattern: dispatches anti\.browser\.tabs\.list under its own name

rows.title: 23 anti.* routing rows redirect a name the catalogue already registers, silently substituting the target's semantics for the server's
rows.evidence: `node scripts/check-mcp-budget-dominance.mjs` reports 23 shadowing rows at HEAD (anti.browser.tabs.create, .activate, .close, navigate, reload, anti.inspect.dom, …). The server registers an `anti.*` alias for each of them, so the routing row — not the server — decides which implementation runs; several anti.* aliases are independent reimplementations with different defaults, so a row's removal is a behaviour change that needs its own proof. anti.browser.tabs.list was one instance of this shape and is fixed: it routed to browser.list-tabs (session-scoped) while the alias it bypassed is window-wide by default.

predicate.reVerifyWith: run node scripts/check-mcp-budget-dominance.mjs and diff the reported shadowing set against the previous sweep; retire a row only after an omp-mcp-adapter case proves the dispatched name change is behaviour-preserving

rows.title: The clone campaign's measured viewports produce no adjudicable verdict: anti.visual.compare's normalization apply exceeds its 15 s bound, so capture.valid is false and every desktop/tablet case is CAPTURE_INVALID
rows.evidence: `.canary/15-pages/_verdicts.json` (run campaign-e2214e66, 2026-09-10T16:52:04Z) records 3 cases and no verdict: 390 REFUSED/MOBILE_BUNDLE_ABSENT, and 1440 + 1024 COMPLETED/INCONCLUSIVE/CAPTURE_INVALID with captureValid=false, visual=INCONCLUSIVE, mismatchPercentage=100 and artifacts.referencePng/clonePng=null. `page-01-home/attempts/attempt-96a175b8-f1bb-437b-9467-accc53d2e661/evidence/summary.json` names the cause for both: visual.reason = "Reversible normalization could not be applied on tab '<tabId>': Visual compare normalization apply (<tabId>) exceeded its 15000ms bound". The same record shows the structure matched exactly at both widths (refDocH/cloneDocH 5546/5546 and 5422/5422, sections 15/15, cards 83/83, overflowX 0/0) while capture.valid was false with exists=false, bytes=0 — yet the standalone PNGs exist on disk (1024: 1.76 MB / 2.00 MB, 1440: 2.36 MB / 2.62 MB). So the clone's structure was measured and matches; the raster verdict is what cannot be produced. scripts/lib/evidence-provenance.mjs:197 is what turns captureValid=false into CAPTURE_INVALID.

predicate.lastVerifiedBy: artifact replay of .canary/15-pages/_verdicts.json and the attempt summary (2026-09-11)
predicate.reVerifyWith: re-run the campaign and require _verdicts.json to contain at least one case whose verdict is PASS or FAIL; a run that measures viewports but adjudicates none now exits non-zero (NO_ADJUDICATED_CASE), so an exit 0 is the evidence that this row is done

rows.title: The committed campaign cannot verify the 390 viewport: it requires clone/mobile/index.html but no mobile clone bundle is ever produced, so every mobile case is refused with MOBILE_BUNDLE_ABSENT
rows.closedBy: The working tree builds the mobile bundle: the 390 readiness-floor pass writes reference-mobile.html and a second build-clone.mjs run writes <attempt>/clone/mobile. Proved by inspection only — the producer has not been exercised (no mobile/ directory exists under .canary/15-pages, and the recorded run predates it), so the row stays closed on the tree marker and reopens if the producer is removed. The verdict still requires a re-run: scripts/lib/campaign-verdicts.mjs treats a requested REFUSED case as incomplete, so the next campaign either produces mobile cases or fails loudly.
rows.evidence: `find .canary/15-pages -type d -name mobile` is empty and `scripts/lib`/`build-clone.mjs` contains no reference to mobile, while `.canary/tools/viewport-run.mjs:519-526` requires `<attempt>/clone/mobile/index.html` for a mobile viewport and `.canary/tools/fifteen-pages-run.mjs:773` records the refusal. scripts/lib/campaign-verdicts.mjs:129 declares MOBILE_BUNDLE_ABSENT and treats a REFUSED case as incomplete, so a campaign that requests 390 can never exit 0 — verified by replaying the recorded run through computeRunExit (code 1 INCOMPLETE_CASES, detail MOBILE_BUNDLE_ABSENT@page-1:390). The working copy adds a producer (mobile reference dump at the 390 readiness floor plus a second build-clone.mjs pass into clone/mobile) which is not committed at HEAD.
